AbstractText.Label: INTRODUCTION
AbstractText.content: Chronic low back pain is a common condition. A new intervention that is popular in sports has been used in patients with low back pain. This technique is based on the use of elastic tapes that are fixed on the skin of patients using different tensions and is named Kinesio Taping Method. Although this intervention has been widely used, to date the evidence of its effectiveness is lacking.

AbstractText.Label: RESEARCH QUESTION
AbstractText.content: Is the application of the Kinesio Taping Method according to the treatment manual (with convolutions in neutral position) more efficacious than a simple application without convolutions in patients with chronic low back pain?

AbstractText.Label: DESIGN
AbstractText.content: Two-arm randomised controlled trial with a blinded assessor.

AbstractText.Label: PARTICIPANTS AND SETTING
AbstractText.content: 148 patients with chronic low back pain from two outpatient physiotherapy clinics in Brazil.

AbstractText.Label: INTERVENTION
AbstractText.content: 8 sessions of Kinesio Taping according to the Kinesio Taping Method treatment manual (ie, 10-15% tension with the treated muscles in stretching position and with convolutions in neutral).

AbstractText.Label: CONTROL
AbstractText.content: 8 sessions of Kinesio Taping having no convolutions in neutral (0% tension) with the treated muscles in resting position.

AbstractText.Label: MEASUREMENTS
AbstractText.content: Clinical outcomes (pain intensity, disability and global impression of recovery) will be obtained in assessments that will be performed at 4 weeks and 3 months after randomisation.

AbstractText.Label: ANALYSIS
AbstractText.content: The effects of the intervention will be calculated through linear mixed models following intention-to-treat principles.

AbstractText.Label: DISCUSSION
AbstractText.content: This is the largest study aimed to investigate the hypothesised mechanism behind the Kinesio Taping application in patients with chronic low back pain. The results of this study will contribute to a better understanding about the mechanisms of action of this widely applied therapeutic modality.
